scope: Corollary 7.1 (Order-oblivious selection with full-seed visibility) of the manuscript “One Sample Suffices for Matroid Prophet Inequalities against an Almighty Adversary” (preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/final.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 111 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4bcbebba49132012), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each known finite labeled matroid M = (E, I), there is one measurable randomized online rule SM with the following property. Fix any vector w ∈ [0, ∞)E of finite nonnegative weights before all rule and arrival randomness. Without knowing w, the rule draws its complete initial seed Q, independently of a uniformly random permutation σ of E, and fixes a possibly random prefix length K before any arrival. It observes the first K label–weight pairs of σ in order and rejects those labels. After this ordered prefix is observed and before any suffix arrival, an adversary may know M, the entire fixed vector w, the ordered prefix, and the complete seed Q, including K, the branch choice, and unused coins. It may choose any measurable permutation τ of the remaining labels as a function of this information. The rule is not told the future suffix order and decides irrevocably at each suffix arrival while maintaining an independent set. Writing AS for its accepted set, for every such adversary, E   X e∈AS we   ≥ 2−293 OPTM (w). (7.1) The expectation is over the rule seed and random prefix, and over any adversary randomization. The adversary cannot alter the random-prefix law or choose the weights after observing the seed or prefix.
